summary: Correct expression: `Math.max(a, c) < Math.min(b, d)`. The common `a < d && c < b` fails when one interval is empty and its point lies strictly inside the other, e.g. [1,1) vs [0,2) returns true but [1,1) is empty. Touching intervals [0,1) and [1,2) correctly give false under the corrected expression.
evidence: Definition: [a,b) and [c,d) overlap iff some x satisfies a<=x<b and c<=x<d, i.e. max(a,c) <= x < min(b,d). Such x exists iff max(a,c) < min(b,d) (take x = max(a,c)). This is an exact equivalence, no nonemptiness assumption needed.
Counterexample to a < d && c < b: a=1,b=1,c=0,d=2. Then 1<2 && 0<1 is true, but [1,1) is empty so there is no overlap. Corrected: max(1,0)=1 < min(1,2)=1 is false.

Why the common form fails: a<d && c<b equals max(a,c)<min(b,d) only when a<b and c<d also hold; it silently assumes both intervals are nonempty. Equivalent long form: a < b && c < d && a < d && c < b.
Touching endpoints: [0,1) vs [1,2): max(0,1)=1 < min(1,2)=1 is false, so touching is nonoverlap as required.
Node brute force over all integer a<=b, c<=d in [0,4] (225 cases) against a grid-search reference: corrected expression 0 mismatches; common expression 20 mismatches, first at [a,b,c,d]=[0,2,1,1].
